355 discoveries from 2020 to 2026

About AI discoveries in computer science

This selection contains 355 catalog entries dated 20 Feb 2020 to 18 Nov 2026. 354 include structured evidence annotations describing reported tests, the AI contribution and remaining limits. Missing annotations mean those details have not been structured here, not that a study lacks evidence.

Dates follow the catalog publication policy. Coverage is selected and incomplete; entries can overlap or describe several results. Counts do not measure independent discoveries, clinical benefit or worldwide research output. Read the selection and evidence policy or compare catalog coverage by year and field.

Discoveries

18 Nov 2026OpenAI

OpenAI models help reduce circuit area in the Jalapeño inference chip

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: OpenAI estimates that AI-proposed changes cut standard-cell area by about 13% in the vector unit and 10% in the matrix unit. OpenAI reports that the optimizations were verified during silicon bring-up. The August announcement reported chip-level performance, while this November account provides the unit-level area estimates.

Technology: OpenAI reasoning models

Editorial relevance 60 computer science Original source Suggest a correction

Publication: Announcement only · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
OpenAI engineers used models to propose arithmetic, circuit and pipeline changes. The account identifies o3-mini in early work and does not assign the full savings to one model.
Test and result
OpenAI reports engineering verification and silicon bring-up.
Limitation / still unknown
The aggregate area savings are company estimates. Independent replication and model-by-model contributions were not reported.

13 Nov 2026Affiliation not stated in the reviewed material

AI-Assisted Failure Prediction on Postoperative X-Rays: A Head-to-Head Comparison with Consultant Trauma Surgeons

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: A prospectively assembled 466-patient application cohort (104 fixation failures) was classified from postoperative radiographs by a ResNet-50 trained on a disjoint 200-patient cohort. AI sensitivity was 96.15% and specificity 98.90%, exceeding the three surgeons numerically; the strongest surgeon difference was not significant. This supports an adjunct diagnostic result, pending external prospective validation. This supports an adjunct diagnostic result, not external prospective validation.

Technology: ResNet-50 image classifier

Editorial relevance 53 computer science Original source Suggest a correction

Publication: Preprint · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
ResNet-50 reads postoperative X-rays and classifies fixation failure against clinical outcome; AI supplies the diagnostic prediction.
Test and result
PDF Results pp.6–8: 466 patients, 104 failures; AI classified 458/466 (98.28% accuracy); paired surgeon analysis and comparison with strongest surgeon reported.
Limitation / still unknown
Same-cohort paired human comparison and a separately trained cohort support diagnostic performance; same centers and authors’ stated need for external prospective validation limit transportability.

11 Nov 2026Independent research

An unstated country representation guides Qwen’s capital answers

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: In a controlled two-step geography task, researchers changed a representation of a country that was never named in the prompt. At the city token, the intervention redirected Qwen2.5-7B to the paired country’s capital in 79% of 1,038 pairs. The country was also readable later in the prompt, where the intervention had no effect at the tested layers. This experiment is reported in the November 11 preprint version.

Technology: Qwen2.5-7B, cross-fitted country subspaces

Family Qwen: profile · models page

Editorial relevance 53 computer science Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Preprint · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
Country subspaces were estimated on one half of the pretrained Qwen2.5-7B city examples, then used in a controlled intervention on matched held-out city examples.
Test and result
The preregistered intervention compared held-out matched city pairs against random and copied-embedding subspaces, whole-state replacement, and same-country pairs.
Limitation / still unknown
The test concerns one model and a constrained task on cities the model already answered correctly. Other tasks and weak latent signals remain unestablished.

8 Nov 2026Affiliation not stated in the reviewed material

Decomposing Earth Embeddings with Sparse Autoencoders

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: Sparse autoencoders decomposed AlphaEarth and Tessera Earth-observation embeddings into sparse features. At matched sparsity they reconstructed the embeddings better than PCA, ICA, NMF and other baselines. Some feature-specificity measures also appeared with a frozen random decoder, so the result supports learned reconstruction quality rather than new geographic discoveries.

Technology: Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) applied to AlphaEarth and Tessera embeddings

Editorial relevance 53 computer science Original source Suggest a correction

Publication: Preprint · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
Sparse autoencoders transform dense Earth-observation embeddings into sparse feature codes; evaluation compared reconstruction, concept alignment and spatial scale against PCA, ICA, NMF and frozen random-decoder baselines.
Test and result
At matched sparsity, trained SAEs reconstructed AlphaEarth and Tessera embeddings better than the tested baselines. Sparse features aligned with fewer reference concept groups and carried more variance at fine spatial scales; a frozen random decoder shared those latter properties.
Limitation / still unknown
This is a representation evaluation; application demonstrations are not yet reliable enough for practical use, and no newly established geographic classes are claimed.

Not All Layers Are Equal in Image-to-Video Transfer

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding / tested result: Across four video-native model families and two pretraining paradigms, the study found that temporal sensitivity changes with transformer depth and differs between vision-only and vision-language models. Its STRAP layer-placement rule improved accuracy by up to 11.8% across four fine-grained action-recognition benchmarks, with fewer trainable parameters; these are benchmark results.

Technology: Video-native image-to-video transformer representations

Editorial relevance 47 computer science Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Preprint · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
Layer-wise temporal-sensitivity analysis of video foundation models motivated STRAP, a training-free rule that assigns spatial and temporal adapters to different layer ranges.
Limitation / still unknown
The study evaluates the reported models and datasets only; broader generalization and real-world deployment outcomes were not established.

Learned agents performed each task under original and edited natural-language instructions. Their repeated scores supplied the null replay and the held-out comparison.
Test and result
The authors tested three optimizers on three benchmarks. Test and result
The experiment held the four-statement evidence size and prompt fixed. 29 Sep 2021Not stated in the abstract reviewed

Prediction of storage time in different seafood based on color values with artificial neural network modeling.

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: A one-hidden-layer, 30-neuron feedforward ANN uses seafood colour coordinates (L*, a*, b*) to predict storage time. The primary paper compiled 205 literature datapoints and evaluated the model on an additional 45 literature datapoints from other seafood studies; the article reports R²=0.81 for the selected topology and a predicted/observed regression coefficient of 0.85 (the abstract rounds R² to 0.80). This is a narrow food-quality prediction result, not new measurements, and the pooled literature-derived validation is not prospective field validation.

Technology: A feedforward MLP uses measured L*, a*, b* values as inputs and one hidden layer to output storage time; topology was chosen by comparing R² and MSE.

Editorial relevance 60 computer science Original source Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
A feedforward MLP uses measured L*, a*, b* values as inputs and one hidden layer to output storage time; topology was chosen by comparing R² and MSE.
Test and result
The selected 30-neuron topology reports R²=0.81 and MSE=0.20 during optimization; the paper separately reports a predicted/observed regression coefficient of 0.85 (abstract R² rounded to 0.80).
Limitation / still unknown
205 literature experiments were split into 145/30/30 train/test/validation; a distinct additional 45 literature datapoints from other species/studies were also used as validation. The evidence is pooled retrospective data, not prospective measured validation, and species/process heterogeneity limits generalization.
